cues.text: Hi Zach! I heard you passed your driving test! Congratulations!
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: Thanks Olivia! I passed just last week.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: It feels great to be independent and driving on my own!
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: I really want to take driving lessons, but I haven’t been able to find a driving school that will give lessons during the weekends . So I have to miss any classes at college.
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: The driving school that I used was brilliant and really flexible with their teaching hours. It’s really close to school.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: It’s really close to school. The address is 67 King’s Road - that’s 67-KING-apostrophe-S Road.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: Oh that’s perfect! I don’t like the idea of driving around busy streets.
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: Did your teacher make you drive in urban areas or did he mainly teach you on roads in the countryside?
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: My teacher said that I had to learn on both in order to become a good and experienced driver.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: We would start in the city centre and then drive north above the city.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: He sounds like a good teacher.
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: Would you mind giving me his contact details so I can ask him for lessons?
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: Of course! My mother’s friend Daniel Smith referred me to him. His name is Allen Sutcliffe.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: Could you spell the surname please?
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: S-U-T-C-L-I-double F-E.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: Thanks for helping me out, I’ll give him a call tomorrow.
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: I don’t know if I should learn in a manual or automatic car.
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: How do I decide?
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: I wasn’t sure which type of car to learn in either.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: In the end I chose to learn in a manual car because once you’ve learnt how to drive manually you can drive automatic as well.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: Most cars on the road are automatic nowadays.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: OK, I think I’ll learn with a manual car too then.
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: Hopefully the teacher will be able to give me lessons in the evenings after school!
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: It would be much better if you take the lessons during the day.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: It will be far easier for you to learn when there is enough daylight to clearly see everything going on around you.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: But you need to be an experienced driver to drive safely at night.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: How frustrating! I was hoping I wouldn’t have to take lessons during the weekends! You’re right though, safety comes first!
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: Speaking of safety, you should wait until summer to start learning!
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: It’s really difficult and dangerous to drive in the wind and rain as a learner so you should definitely wait until the weather is sunny and dry.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: OK, that’s perfect, actually!
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: It will give me some time to save up some money to pay for the lessons.
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: Tell me about it! I had to work for months before I had enough money saved up!
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: It was worth all the work when I finally got my driving license though!
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: The whole process is so expensive! How much did it cost you in the end?
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: Well, each half hour lesson cost $30 and then the final test cost $50. In total it cost me about $300.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: Gosh, it’s pretty expensive! How did you find the test? Was it really difficult?
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: No, it wasn’t too bad, and the man was really calm and friendly.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: I knew that I would have to perform two parking manoeuvres during the test, so I practised them a lot beforehand and that really helped!
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: The test used to last 40 minutes, but it changed a bit.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: For the first 20 minutes of the test he gave me directions and I had to just drive around and then the last 10 minutes was for demonstrating the manoeuvres, so the test is 30 minutes in total.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: OK, great, I’ll remember that! Do you have any more advice?
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: It’s really good to practise driving a lot outside of driving lessons as well.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: Whenever my parents were running errands on the weekends I would offer to drive them.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: My driving teacher also told me to buy a notebook to write down everything that I’ve learnt in it like a  diary.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: Haha, that sounds boring, but I’ll do it if it helps.
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: I found it really useful! Before my test I read through everything I had written down and it reminded me of a lot of things that I had forgotten about!
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: It’s really helpful for the theory test as well because there’s so much information to remember for it.
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: That’s great, Zach! Thanks for your help!
cues.speaker: OLIVIA

cues.text: No problem, see you at school!
cues.speaker: ZACH

cues.text: Bye!
cues.speaker: OLIVIA
